My typical week includes several hours traveling between Indiana and Washington, which provides time for reading. Here are ten books I greatly enjoyed in 2023:

▪️Chip War by Chris Miller – Why computer chips are mission critical to our national defense and economic welfare, and the story behind the doers and dreamers (and, yes, the government policies) which brought us these critical inputs.

▪️The Coming Wave by Mustafa Suleyman – The author compellingly argues that Artificial Intelligence and Synthetic Biology are the foundational technologies which will positively transform our way of life, if we can strike the right balance between enjoying the fruits of innovation and managing the downside risks.

▪️Sea Power by Adm. James Stavridis, USN (Ret.) – Throughout history, strategists have debated whether land or sea powers hold the geopolitical keys to geopolitical primacy. Drawing on a lifetime of professional training and experience, Stavridis makes the case for naval power. He takes the reader on a tour of the world’s most contested waters.

▪️The Avoidable War by Kevin Rudd – The former Australian Prime Minister and current U.S. Ambassador offers a sweeping presentation of modern Chinese power, its influences and influencers, and how the West can prevail while avoiding a military confrontation.

▪️The Peacemaker by William Inboden – A welcome arrival as Republicans debate whether to embrace or move on from Ronald Reagan’s legacy. By documenting how the 40th president helped America win the Cold War, Inboden’s book provides an answer: Conservatives should revive Reagan’s leadership and character while remembering how he broke with the past to forge his own path, remaining true to his principles along the way.

▪️On Grand Strategy by John Lewis Gaddis – Historian and professor of the popular Yale seminar “Studies in Grand Strategy,” Gaddis presents selected observations and experiences of history’s leaders and thinkers to equip today’s leaders to think strategically.

▪️Red Carpet: Hollywood, China and the Global Battle for Cultural Supremacy by Erich Schwartzel – The Wall Street Journal’s Hollywood reporter walks us through the Chinese Communist Party’s coercive efforts to guide the production and distribution of content by America’s beloved movie industry. Schwartzel names names as Hollywood’s unclean hands have become instruments of the CCP’s domestic and foreign propaganda machine.

▪️Quiet by Susan Cain – Cain exposes and examines America’s cultural predilection for superficiality over depth, stimulation over solitude, loudness over quiet. She makes a compelling case for rebalancing our bias for extroversion over introversion so that individuals, organizations, and society might realize their full potential.

▪️Out On a Limb: Selected Writing (1989-2021) by Andrew Sullivan – Fiercely independent conservative columnist and podcaster Andrew Sullivan gives modern conservatives and liberals alike a clinic in critical thinking, intellectual curiosity, and important yet accessible writing.

▪️How Soccer Explains the World by Franklin Foer – The talented Atlantic writer traveled the world to immerse himself in ten stories about “the Beautiful Game” which reveal the deeper cultural, political, and economic forces shaping our times.
